questions.q_en: A clock is set right at 7 p.m. The clock gains 12 minutes in every 3 hours. If, later the day, the actual time is 10: 15 p.m., then what will be the time shown in the watch?
questions.solution_en:
The duration between 7 p.m. to 10: 20 p.m. = 3 hours 15 minutes

According to the question, in 3 hours it gains 12 minutes.

In 1 hours it gains (12/3 = 4) minutes.

In 1 minute, it gains (4/60) minutes = (1/15) minutes.

And, in 15 minutes, it gains (15 x (1/15)) minutes = 1 minute

Then, in 3 hours 15 minutes, it gains (4 x 3 + 1) = 13 minutes

Therefore, the time shown by the faulty watch will be = 10: 15 p.m. + 13 minutes = 10: 28 p.m.

69 X Number of vowels in TAME

= 69 x 2 = 138

ADMIRE---

A (reverse position = 26) + D (reverse position = 23) + M (reverse position = 14) + I (reverse position = 18) + R(reverse position = 9) + E (reverse position = 22) = 112

112 X Number of vowels in ADMIRE

112 x 3 = 336

FUN---

F (reverse position = 21) + U (reverse position = 6) + N (reverse position = 13) = 40

40 x Number of vowels in FUN

= 40 x 1 = 40

questions.q_en:
In the question given below, a passage is given followed by three statements. Read the passage and answer the question that follows.

Statement: The government should get the pubs, movie halls and stores shut down at 12 am to reduce crimes.

Arguments:

I. Yes, this will not leave any scope for criminals lurking in the streets at night to commit crimes.

II. No, this will instead make it difficult for people to go out at night for any important work.

III. No, this will deprive the people of enjoying their late nights by hanging out at pubs and movie halls.

Which of the above arguments is a/are strong argument(s)?
options_en: Only II and III are strong arguments
None of I, II and III are strong arguments
Only I is a strong argument
Only II is a strong argument
questions.solution_en: Shutting down the pubs, movie halls, stores, etc. is not a solution to curb crimes. It will further make people who may have to go out at night for any work vulnerable to criminals. So, (I) is not a strong argument while (II) is. (III) is not strong either as entertainment is not the prime concern. Hence, (d) is correct.

questions.q_en:
Which two signs and numbers need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

528 ÷ 9 - 16 x 4 + 156 = 120
questions.solution_en:
Option (a):

528 ÷ 9 - 16 x 4 + 156 = 120

After interchange:

528 ÷ 9 + 16 x 156 - 4 = 120

58.6 + 2496 - 4 = 120

2550.6 is not equal to 120

Thus this option is not correct.

Option (b):

528 ÷ 9 - 16 x 4 + 156 = 120

After interchange:

528 ÷ 4 + 16 x 9 - 156 = 120

132 + 144 - 156 = 120

276 - 156 = 120

120 = 120

Thus, this option is correct.

Option (c):

528 ÷ 9 - 16 x 4 + 156 = 120

After interchange:

156 x 9 - 16 ÷ 4 + 528 = 120

1404 - 4 + 528 = 120

1928 is not equal to 120

Thus, this option is correct.

Option (d):

528 ÷ 9 - 16 x 4 + 156 = 120

After interchange:

528 ÷ 16 - 9 + 4 x 156 = 120

33 - 9 + 624 = 120

648 is not equal to 120

Thus, this option is incorrect.
